lessons.title: Build a rounded part from measured pieces, not from a three-view hull
lessons.statement: A visual hull made from three silhouettes cannot carry rounded cross-sections: it comes out boxy, and a loft through the silhouette extents bulges between the views. Build the part from pieces measured on each view, and keep the hull only as a measuring instrument (silhouette overlap).

evidence.summary: Clay renders of the hull were boxy; the rounded view-loft read as a beehive with curtains.

measured.metric: silhouette IoU of the part-built version

toolmaking.trigger: the hull looked wrong in clay renders
toolmaking.caught: three silhouettes cannot define rounded sections
toolmaking.why: the hull stayed useful as a measure once it stopped being the shape

lessons.title: Distance checks must be two-sided
lessons.statement: A one-sided distance (build to reference only) passes a build that is missing whole regions. Measure both directions and report the worst of the two, per region.

evidence.summary: The one-sided check passed while the two-sided one found large voids at the ear bases.

proof.planted_defect: a deleted patch of the surface (a void the one-sided measure cannot see)
